name: Arnulf the Firekeeper
notes: Germanic village firekeeper. Laughs with his whole body. Resents Corvinus, likes Varro.
gm_notes: Keeps the village fires and the fire-related rituals. His laughter is genuine and frequent; he finds Romans consistently baffling and endearing. His resentment of Corvinus is personal -- Roman soldiers damaged a sacred fire site during a previous patrol, and Corvinus's response was to blame the tribe. His warmth toward Varro stems from a specific incident (Varro stopped three soldiers from desecrating the same site later; Arnulf saw it). Offers news from the Limes to party members who treat him as a peer. Entry point: bringing trade goods, sharing a meal, working alongside him physically. Voice line: 'Romans eat like wolves: fast, suspicious, grateful afterward.'
objective: Keep the village fires and the tribal memory they carry.
goal: Get Roman acknowledgement that the sacred fire site will not be disturbed again.
agenda: Assess this specific group of Romans before deciding how much to share.
secret: He knows exactly which Roman officer gave the desecration order. It was not Varro.
